findings.claim: Goal 2 promises to 'expose post-snapshot drift and bypass as residual risks', but the state machine and P14 instead make drift a blocking, fail-closed precondition ('any drift expires the bundle') re-observed at the charge boundary. The design never states that its protocol eliminates the check-to-charge race; it leaves the same irreducible race in place and labels it residual, so the claimed mitigation is not the mitigation the enforcement model specifies.

locator.value: 3.1 Design goals (Goal 2); 5.1 Critical rule; 5.3 Enforcement boundary and residual race; 7 P14 Bundle freshness

findings.evidence_excerpt: Goal 2: 'Ensure every known admission failure is detected before attempt charge; expose post-snapshot drift and bypass as residual risks.' Section 5.1: 'Every live predicate must be re-observed immediately at the charge boundary; any drift expires the bundle.' Section 5.3: 'An irreducible check-to-charge race remains when external state can change between observation and mutation.' P14: 'All current hashes/native states still equal the sealed bundle immediately before commit' -> 'EXPIRED; re-prepare uncharged'.
findings.impact: An implementer can read 'expose drift as residual risk' as permission to charge once the bundle is sealed, contradicting the mandatory pre-commit re-observation in 5.1/P14 and potentially permitting charge under drift; or can read the protocol as eliminating a race it does not. Goal-level ambiguity about whether drift blocks or is merely reported is the charge-ambiguity class the scope requires to be material.
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite Goal 2 to state separately: (a) drift observed before commit blocks charge via EXPIRED; (b) the check-to-charge race after the last observation is an irreducible residual risk reported to the HUMAN and not claimed eliminated.

findings.claim: The root-cause evidence basis is bound only to a self-declared hash in the design's prose and is not registered in its own Sources of Truth or artifact registry. Section 2 asserts the immutable run-002 failure-model snapshot is SHA-256 434f1613751d8a2b5b8813936404e4567e698ea4ace88ed74863e2a56e4d8b86, while the independently pinned failure-model bytes carried in this review packet hash to 8dc7a65b40883d8bc020ed4ee41fa45048e134c9478b9a1a5346c76a44f76c8d; no owning command re-verifies this pin during admission prepare.

locator.value: 2. Evidence basis and root-cause classification; 2.1; 6 Immutable AdmissionBundle (receipts)

findings.evidence_excerpt: 'The evidence-bound failure model used for v2 is the immutable run-002 snapshot snapshots/failure-model, SHA-256 434f1613751d8a2b5b8813936404e4567e698ea4ace88ed74863e2a56e4d8b86; the mutable Workspace path is only its working source.' The bundle receipts enumerate plan_format, plan_semantics, execution_strict, dependency_acceptance, source_integrity, aip_asc_transition, command_capability, coordinator_quiescence, team_authority, goal_activation, reviewer_availability and budget_reserve, but no root-cause/evidence-model pin.
findings.impact: RC-SYSTEM-01, the counterfactual coverage table and the WBS entry criteria depend on an evidence pin no reviewer or admission receipt can independently re-derive. If different bytes are authoritative, admission and later WBS citations rest on unverifiable evidence; per the design's own NOT_READY rule for missing/stale/ambiguous material this blocks or invalidates admission rather than being a harmless typo.
findings.recommended_action: Register the run-002 failure model as a named immutable evidence artifact with exact path, hash and immutability owner; add an admission receipt/P-predicate that re-hashes it during prepare; fail closed on mismatch; reconcile 434f1613... vs 8dc7a65b... before any WBS build.

findings.claim: The transition-ownership rule (generated control artifacts change only through declared owning commands) is stated only for .current_step.json and ASC; other mutable mission-control artifacts (execution ledger and its current projection, progress/report renderings, admission/charge records) have no equivalent prohibition on manual or undeclared edits, and migration 9.2 step 7 authorizes writing a separate current projection without naming its owning command.

locator.value: 10. AIP/ASC generated-artifact policy; 9.2 Migration protocol step 7; 6 Immutable AdmissionBundle

findings.evidence_excerpt: Section 10: '`.current_step.json` and ASC are generated projections owned by declared AIWS commands. Every WBS task requiring a pointer/ASC change must declare the exact `run_aip.py start|resume|step` argv that produces it. Manual ASC body edits are forbidden as acceptance evidence.' Section 9.2 step 7: 'Write a small current projection separately from immutable historical evidence when the contract permits it.'
findings.impact: A ledger, projection or charge-record change outside a declared owning command is neither declared, detected, nor evidenced by an admission receipt, so the bundle can seal READY while a mutable control surface was altered by an undeclared path - the same undeclared-transition class the design names as a contributing condition, only partially closed.
findings.recommended_action: Generalize the policy to every generated/mutable mission-control artifact: one declared owning command each, manual/unowned edits invalid as evidence and blocking admission, migration projection written only by a named command, and a re-hashed receipt per artifact during prepare.

findings.claim: Section 7.1, the normative contingency rule, identifies the current revision as 'v32' while the document under review is design v2 and its own HOLD semantics already forbid any build or charge; the misapplied revision reference makes it unclear which revision a binding HUMAN ceiling decision must name.
findings.evidence_excerpt: 'Because v32 currently has no slack, no WBS may be built or admitted until the HUMAN records a ceiling/reallocation and contingency decision bound to the exact WBS revision and hash.'
findings.impact: The HUMAN ceiling/reallocation decision and WBS-revision binding are authority-critical; an incorrect revision identifier in the single clause holding the mission frozen invites a decision bound to the wrong revision and muddies the audit trail of which revision the hold applies to.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the revision reference, state the holding rule against the actual current revision (v3) and the exact design/WBS hash, and re-verify it names the same revision as the section 16 entry criteria.
